### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **36** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx`  _(via unit_price (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via fieldLabel (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via unit_price (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, bridged from symbol resolveI18nService — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, bridged from symbol resolveI18nService — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, bridged from symbol resolveI18nService — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 33 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f6c619329a447f31859da9cad75f6084c430c810` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `61f346e551b77ff956035099ed13f9a0698fa89f` — the merge of head `9852ed899dfb3c55df2b79ffbec7379711b925b6` into base `f6c619329a447f31859da9cad75f6084c430c810`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 61f346e551b77ff956035099ed13f9a0698fa89f && git checkout 61f346e551b77ff956035099ed13f9a0698fa89f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f6c619329a447f31859da9cad75f6084c430c810 9852ed899dfb3c55df2b79ffbec7379711b925b6 && git checkout -B drift-repro f6c619329a447f31859da9cad75f6084c430c810 && git merge --no-ff 9852ed899dfb3c55df2b79ffbec7379711b925b6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f6c619329a447f31859da9cad75f6084c430c810
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f6c619329a447f31859da9cad75f6084c430c810` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `50c3929ba378fb3f724a572830a7e96aadc74eae`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/not-null-refusal-error.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-not-null-refusal.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/driver-fault-boundary-redaction.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-insert-duplicate-record.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-update-duplicate-record.test.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.not-null-label.test.ts, packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/not-null-refusal-label.ts (removed), packages/rest/src/not-null-refusal-label.test.ts (removed), packages/rest/src/data-not-null-field-label-24715.test.ts, packages/rest/src/data-not-null-hint-20963.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-not-null-refusal-24768.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.anchor-parity.test.ts + packages/types/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/core.ts, packages/rest/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts, packages/types/src/validation-failure.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, packages/types/src/driver-fault-redaction.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, packages/rest/src/error-response.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts, docs/adr/0112-error-code-vocabulary-and-ledger.md, docs/adr/0113-required-write-contract-vs-column-constraint.md, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .changeset/24768-not-null-refusal-every-door.md (prose face)

Inputs: card #24768 body and all four comments (claim 6410180146, amendments 6410372925 and 6411384588, dev report 6412700035); PR #26026 body, file list (17 paths) and net diff at this head; the head's check-runs. Read-only: no worktree, no build, no test, no gate re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The Clause-② declaration is well-formed and right.** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing: …)` is read by `readClause2Line` as `value: yes, arm: narrowing` (the parenthetical's first token is the arm; trailing prose is tolerated), the combination `clause2-line.mjs` documents as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another". Both facts are measured on the committed tree:
- Widening (`yes` is required): `packages/types/src/index.ts:98` is `export * from './data-error-classification.js'`, so the new `export function notNullViolationSite(error)` is a new member of `@objectstack/types`' published entry.
- Narrowing (the `(narrowing)` arm is required): the same entry loses `notNullRefusalSite` and `relabelNotNullRefusal` (both `export`ed on `origin/main` at `data-error-classification.ts:2155` and `:2181`); the dispatcher `/data` wire moves `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` to `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`; `RestServer` `/data` POST/PATCH drops the `hint` key and adds `label` to `fields[0]` for a declared field. ADR-0112's own precedent (#9266 amendment) names a retirement of this kind "accept-set narrowing".
- No new error code: `VALIDATION_FAILED` is a ledger member (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts:302`); nothing is added to `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` or `StandardErrorCode`, so the "new code ⇒ yes" rule is not what makes this `yes`.
- The PR body and the changeset carry the identical line, bare, at line start, and `Metadata-protocol: none` beside it on both. The claim's `no` was wrong once the amended surface added the `@objectstack/types` export change; the dev measured the departure and declared it. The face is therefore the narrowing face, which is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (`record-recognisers --paths` finds no schema or governed path in the file list and defers to the `Clause-②` arm).

**One answer per declared-field NOT NULL refusal, door by door** (status and `code` read from the exits' code and the PR's pins):
- Engine (`engine.ts`, five driver exits: both autonumber-retry sites, `bulkCreate`/per-row fallback, by-id `update`, `updateMany`): `envelopeDriverWriteRefusal` composes the existing `envelopeUniqueViolation` first, then `envelopeNotNullViolation`; a NOT NULL refusal whose column the object's field map holds (own-property check, same-table check) leaves as `NotNullRefusalError extends ValidationError`, `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'`, one field error built by the validator's `buildFieldError` with the engine's `validationMessageContext` (label from bundle, then `label`, then API name; `required` on insert, `required_cleared` on update), driver error on `cause`. Pinned in `engine-not-null-refusal.test.ts` (18: every exit, five dialect fixtures, zh-CN/zh parity with the validator's own `required`, and five controls).
- Dispatcher `/data` POST and PATCH (`HttpDispatcher.dispatch()` throws; both exits): `resolveThrownHttpError` treats the validation shape as a declared 400 with `VALIDATION_FAILED` (`thrown-http-error.ts:197-230`); `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` (`plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts:354`) therefore renders `400` with `error.code: VALIDATION_FAILED` and `details.fields`; `dispatcher-plugin.ts:697-701` reads the same `validationFailureDetails` to `VALIDATION_FAILED_STATUS`. Pinned in `dispatcher-not-null-refusal-24768.test.ts` on a real better-sqlite3 store: `hono.status` 400, `error.code`, `error.message` from `renderValidationMessage`, `details.fields` with `label`, and `validationFailureDetails(thrown).code`; was 500 on `main` (red first, 3 failed).
- Actions door (`domains/actions.ts:1040-1113`): a `ValidationError` is not an `unexpectedFault` (`validationFailureDetails` matches) and exits `errorFromThrown(err, 400)`, so `error.code` is `VALIDATION_FAILED` with `details.fields`, no `declaredCode`; before, the raw driver error's string `.code` was demoted to `declaredCode` and `error.code` fell to the status-derived `VALIDATION_ERROR` with the driver's text as message. Pinned (status, code, message, fields, `declaredCode` absent, no driver text on the wire).
- `RestServer` POST/PATCH `/data` and `POST /data/:object/batch` rows: `crud-routes.ts` now calls `mapDataError` only; `classifyDataError`'s validation arm (`data-error-classification.ts:1184-1194`) answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `fields` passed through, so `label` rides and no `hint` is added. Pinned in `data-not-null-field-label-24715.test.ts` with `toEqual` on the whole body (keys `code`, `error`, `fields`, `object`), both locales, the batch row's `{ code, message }`, and the undeclared-column control keeping the column sentence plus `hint`.
- Import rows (`core/src/utils/import-runner.ts:521`), the form submit (`form-routes.ts`) and data actions (`data-action-routes.ts`) classify through the same `mapDataError`, and the MCP tool error (`mcp-http-tools.ts:337-343`, `thrownRefusalEnvelope` reads `.code`) now sees `VALIDATION_FAILED` instead of the driver's code. These are the same arm by construction and were not driven on a real store in this PR (the dev says so); see ③.

**Tests assert `code` and `status` per ADR-0112**, never `toThrow()` alone: every door pin above asserts the HTTP status and the nested or flat `code`, and the engine pins assert `.code`, `.name` and the field envelope. The sentence is asked of `renderValidationMessage` in every test, not spelled.

**Driver text does not leak.** The envelope's `message` is the validator's sentence (engine pin: `not.toMatch(/constraint failed|unit_price/)`); the dispatcher and actions pins reject `/constraint failed|SQLITE_/` on the serialised body; the REST batch pin rejects `/constraint failed|unit_price is required/`. `cause` never reaches a wire body (none of the three exits serialises it). At the engine boundary `redactPropagatedDriverFault` (`driver-fault-redaction.ts:1006-1030`) walks the own `cause` property and cuts its statement text; `driver-fault-boundary-redaction.test.ts` pins, for the three NOT NULL shapes × four write doors, `instanceof NotNullRefusalError`, `code`, `fields`, and a `cause` of the raw error's prototype and code. The write-failure log lines log the `cause` (the database's own diagnosis), pinned.

**What is public.** `NotNullRefusalError`, `envelopeNotNullViolation` and `envelopeDriverWriteRefusal` are not exported from `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` or `core.ts`; the public contract a consumer sees is the already-published `ValidationError` (`instanceof` true, `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'`, `fields`). `CrudRouteHost.labelNotNullRefusal` (removed) is on an interface `packages/rest/src/index.ts` does not export, and `RestServer.labelNotNullRefusal` was `private`. The only published-surface movement is in `@objectstack/types`: `+ notNullViolationSite`, `- notNullRefusalSite`, `- relabelNotNullRefusal` (`NotNullRefusalSite` stays). Zero consumers of the two retired names outside the retired REST relabel (the dev's grep of `ui/**`, `examples/**`, hotcrm; the ADR-0087 `runtime-export-retired` gate re-checks the metadata surfaces at the merge base and is green on this head).

**Scope vs the claim.** Every production path is inside the claim plus its two amendments (`packages/objectql/**`, `packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts` and test, the REST relabel retirement and its two call sites, the runtime test, the plugin-auth test pin). No `packages/spec/**`, no production code in `plugin-auth`, no driver package edited (dialect codes are read in `@objectstack/types`, as amendment 6410372925 asked). No pre-write check reads `storage.notNull` (pinned: `required` still refuses before the driver, `driver.create` never called).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/24768-not-null-refusal-every-door.md`: `@objectstack/objectql: patch`, `@objectstack/types: patch`, `@objectstack/rest: patch`. Under ruling A (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone) `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol widening-plus-narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING carriers. Correct. `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-auth` receive tests only and are rightly absent.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing: …)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and the changeset, byte-identical, bare at line start. Correct (①). `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: no spec key, value, type or default moves.
- `**BREAKING**` banner present, naming both facts (export retirement, wire-answer change). The migration is in the body as FROM → TO lines for both retired exports (`notNullRefusalSite(answer)` → `notNullViolationSite(error)`; `relabelNotNullRefusal(...)` → none, write through the engine). The REST wire change (no `hint`, `label` on `fields[0]`, `required_cleared` on PATCH) and the dispatcher 500 → 400 are stated in the body.
- ADR-0087 disposition: exactly one marker, `not-required (runtime-export-retired @objectstack/types#notNullRefusalSite, @objectstack/types#relabelNotNullRefusal) …`; `runtime-export-retired` is a `CATEGORIES` member of `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, the symbols are named in the `package#symbol` form that category reads, and the `Check Changeset` job (which carries the "Require an ADR-0087 disposition" step) is `success` on this head. No stored metadata moves, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the disposition is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Platform-filled columns (dev `open_questions[0]`, needs_decision) — a contract reading, then a product call.** There is no published contract that makes a platform-filled NOT NULL violation answer differently from a caller's. ADR-0113 D1/D2 split `required` (write contract) from `storage.notNull` (column constraint) and say nothing about who fills the column. ADR-0112 keys server-fault handling on the status channel and treats a 5xx as the withholding scope; the one measured posture (ADR-0131 D9, "no organization object, single") is one where the engine deliberately leaves the row organization-less and lets the column refuse, and `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF`'s own description (`injected-system-column-provenance.ts:121`) calls that outcome "a write that names no organization is refused", a refusal, not a fault. In every other posture the engine refuses the same write before the driver as `ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`, a declared 4xx. So on contract grounds option A (as shipped) is consistent, and nothing requires a 500. Whether a hidden, readonly, `system: true` column should surface to a form as `fields[0].code: 'required'` is a product decision; I do not decide it. Recommendation: keep A. Two facts argue against B as written: `sys_user_permission_set` declares `organization_id` itself without `system: true` (`sys-user-permission-set.object.ts:110`), so B would not change the measured case, and B keys behaviour off a flag the injected and the declared spellings of the same column do not share, re-creating a per-declarer split. If the maintainer wants the platform-fault reading, the right seam is the engine's ADR-0131 D9 exit (refuse before the driver in the no-organization-object posture too, with the declared code), not an exclusion in the translation.
2. **Doors not driven on a real store in this PR:** import rows, the public form submit, the generic `/batch`, and MCP. Each reaches the same `ValidationError` arm (`mapDataError` for the REST three; `thrownRefusalEnvelope` for MCP), so the answer follows by construction, but no pin names the NOT NULL class there. Not a defect of this card; a follow-up pin per door would close it.
3. **The undeclared column stays divergent across doors** (REST: `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` column sentence + drift `hint`; dispatcher `/data`: `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`; actions: `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with the driver's text in `message`). Ruling A scoped the translation to "a field the object declares", so this is outside the card, but the card's title ("one answer per refusal across doors") is not fully met for drift. Worth its own card (direction: the dispatcher exits recognising `mapDataError`'s NOT NULL arm, which is the card's option B restricted to that class).
4. **Departures the dev flagged, all accepted here:** (a) `Clause-②` `yes (narrowing)` against the claim's `no` (①, correct); (b) `RestServer`'s declared-field body loses `hint` and reads `required_cleared` on PATCH (the validator's own shape; a wire narrowing, declared under the banner); (c) a drifted column a field still declares is now labelled (`drift_col` control re-pinned with `required_cleared`); (d) the plugin-auth anchor-parity pin moved from the raw driver code to `VALIDATION_FAILED` + `fields [['organization_id','required']]` + `cause.code: SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_NOTNULL` (amendment 6411384588; still proves the column refused the row, distinct from `refused-d9`).
5. **Test deletions and moved pins:** `not-null-refusal-label.test.ts` goes with the module it tested; its label assertions are re-pinned closer to the code (engine test) and at the REST door (24715 test); its "declared column's hint" assertion is dropped as a contract change, declared. `data-not-null-hint-20963.test.ts` loses its PATCH case with a stated reason (a PATCH naming an undeclared field is refused before the driver) and now simulates drift by re-registering the object without the column. The #21274 door sweep skips the NOT NULL × write-door pairs and re-pins them in a block of their own. The duplicate-record controls' NOT NULL fixture now names an undeclared column, so those identity pins keep measuring what they measured.
6. **`statedNotNull` reads `rawCode` before `code`.** A libsql error carrying `rawCode: 1299` reads true, as measured; an error whose `rawCode` were a primary code (19) beside `code: 'SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_NOTNULL'` would read false and leave as the driver threw it (today's answer), never a wrong translation. Fail-closed; noted, not a defect.
7. **Check-runs on this head at record time:** 25 `success`, 8 `skipped`, 0 failed, 12 still `in_progress` with no conclusion: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/8)` through `(8/8)`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · workspace`. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check PR Size`, the claim/branch guards and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are `success`. The landing waits for the remaining twelve to report green; this record judges the contract face and is not a substitute for them.
8. **Dogfood battery** (dev-run, not a check-run): `test/authz-probe-blind-spot.test.ts` is red on `main` since `69fa23d60b` (#25956) per the dev's `grep -c` evidence; not caused here, not fixed here, noted as an out-of-scope finding with a carrier. Not filed; the dogfood seat should card it.
